summary: Feature: Symmetric mirrors two lines, two arcs or two circles about any line, a construction line or the H or V axis, as one relation that stores the two curves and no pairing of their points. Lines pair an end they share with itself and otherwise pair their ends by where they are before each edit, so either line may run either way. A mirror reverses an arc's sweep, so arcs of one direction pair each start with the other's end and arcs of opposite directions pair start with start. Circles pair their centres, and mirrored arcs and circles keep one radius. The relation lowers every pair whole, as point mirrors: an end both curves share is held on the mirror, and circles add one equal-radius row. There is no new equation kind. The relation yields to the rest of the sketch. It lowers after every other relation, and each of its rows is a constraint of its own. A row that only repeats what the curves, fixed values or other relations already keep is solved but not reported as redundant; one that disagrees still conflicts. So two lines kept Horizontal mirror about V, and the freedom left counts only what the mirror adds. A pair that does not reflect yet starts the second curve’s point at the first’s image. So a new mirror moves the second curve onto the first, and arcs settle on the true mirror rather than on another crossing of their circles. The Constrain tool and the selection offers plan it through the shared planner. Two curves of one kind and a line or an axis, picked in any order, offer Symmetric; among three lines the one construction line is the mirror, or else the line picked last. Two kinds, and pairs a mirror cannot map, are refused with the reason. So are lines whose other relations or fixed ends keep them in directions the mirror cannot map, naming those relations; arcs or circles whose fixed radii differ; and point Symmetrics that pair two lines’ ends the other way round from where they lie. The relation is stored only in this form. Point Symmetrics that already hold two lines' ends, or a centre Symmetric of two circles with their Equal radius, show as applied, and Remove removes them. Where other relations keep part of a mirror, such as one point Symmetric, an Equal or a shared end on the mirror, the curve Symmetric joins them. Equal on curves that already mirror is refused. Equal refuses a line with an arc or circle, with the reason. Marks sit on both curves and on the mirror line, and the relation list and inspection name it Symmetric curves. Trim removes a curve Symmetric with either curve it trims and lists it; Split and Extend refuse it while it names the curve.
warning: Potentially breaking for CAD files and agents. Installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions and controller output are not affected. The sketch graph schema gains a second Symmetric shape, { kind: 'symmetric', curveIds, lineId }. Sketches that store it do not open in 0.0.793 or earlier; the CAD format is alpha and carries no compatibility in either direction. Every relation a sketch stores today keeps its meaning and compiles to the same equations: the 0.0.788 equation baseline replays unchanged, byte for byte. Compiled equations gain an optional yields flag, which only a curve Symmetric’s rows carry. Only the TypeScript diagnosis reads it; the native buffers do not carry it. Two circles with a line, picked in the Constrain tool or offered for a selection, now give the curve Symmetric, which also keeps their radii equal. Before, they gave a point Symmetric of their centres. A point and a circle still give the point form, and three lines now also offer Symmetric. A Trim of a mirrored curve now lists the curve Symmetric in removedRelationIds. An agent request that confirms an older list rejects with unconfirmed-sketch-trim-removals and names the expected IDs. The relation editor's Symmetric centers checkbox still mirrors only two circles' centres, and does not show a curve Symmetric of those circles as checked. The worker protocol stays version 7.

checklist.schema: Sketch graph schema change: the symmetric relation gains a curveIds variant, two lines, two arcs or two circles mirrored about the lineId, which names a line or @h or @v. A parse refuses it with invalid-sketch-symmetry, giving the reason, for: two kinds; an axis among the curves; a mirror that is not a line; one curve twice; two circles on one centre; two lines on the same two ends; arcs on the same three points; arcs sharing an end that their directions pair with another point; a shared end off the mirror; and a curve point at an end of the axis line that the curves do not share. Its key sorts curveIds, so either order is one relation. Lowering emits only existing rows: symmetric-midpoint, symmetric-perpendicular, point-on-line for a shared end, and difference for two circles' radii. The lowering context gains each point’s position before the edit, its Coincident identity, and start(pointId, position). start sets a point’s free coordinates where the relation puts them, and the compiler applies those values before solving. Relation definitions gain an optional yields. lowerAll lowers such relations after all the others, in graph order. Each of their equations takes a tag of its own and the equation model’s new optional yields flag; the TypeScript diagnosis reads that flag and never reports such an equation as redundant. Only the curve Symmetric yields, so every other sketch compiles and diagnoses as before. The precision policy gains one role, mirrorPairingTieRelative (1e-9): two lines pair their ends crossed only when that is nearer to each other's mirror images, in summed squared gaps, by more than that fraction, so near ties keep start with start. No existing role changes, so CAD_PRECISION_VERSION stays 1. No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol schema change. The native protocol stays version 7 with the same buffers, and the Rust solver and the committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. The post engine API remains 1 and the saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version or cancellation change. Agent operand change: set-sketch-relation accepts the curveIds form of symmetric. cad_inspect_sketch_constraints names it Symmetric curves, with its own meaning, and lists every point of both curves and the axis line's ends. The relation offers and the Constrain tool give it for two curves of one kind and a line or an axis. Trim's removedRelationIds include a curve Symmetric that names the trimmed curve; Split refuses it with dependent-sketch-split, and Extend refuses it as a dependency. Nothing new runs on pointer moves. A lowering of a curve Symmetric reads the pairing once, which for two lines compares four distances, and the planner reads a selection once. Its direction and fixed-radius checks read the sketch’s relations once for each plan of two curves.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change, and no WebMCP tool added or removed. The symmetric agent summary names lines, arcs and circles, and the WebMCP discovery metadata stays at 51,178 of 51,200 bytes, unchanged. The public agent guide documents the curve form, its pairing, its refusals, the relations recognised as already holding it, the relations it joins and the ones it refuses by name, the Equal refusals, and Trim, Split and Extend. The CAD guide documents picking, marks, mirroring two horizontal lines about V, and refusals. Constrain offers Symmetric for two lines, two arcs or two circles and a line or an axis, in any order. Equal says why a line and an arc or circle cannot be equal.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Saved CAD documents parse as before; nothing is rewritten.
checklist.verification: Equation baseline: the 0.0.788 fixture replays unchanged and is not re-recorded. Every input gives the same compiled models, native answers, graph-check hashes, constraint inspection row hashes and solver attempts, byte for byte. For that, the point Symmetric keeps its recorded agent meaning; the curve form takes its own through a new optional meaningOf on relation definitions, which constraint inspection reads. New tests: cadSketchCurveSymmetry (17) covers nine scenes about the V axis, the H axis, a fixed construction line and a fixed ordinary line. The scenes are: lines; lines running opposite ways; lines sharing an end; arcs; arcs running opposite ways; arcs sharing an end, a centre, or both ends; and circles. For every scene, mirror and pick order it checks the offer and the Constrain tool step, and choosing the mirror among three lines. It also checks the prompts and the pairing, including opposite line directions, opposite arc sweeps, and the pairing tie on each side of mirrorPairingTieRelative. Lowering: every pair whole, after every other relation, each row a yielding constraint of its own: 4, 4, 3, 6, 6, 5, 5, 4 and 3 rows, with the circle radius row. Arcs remove one freedom fewer than their rows, as the second radius follows. A native solve checks the reflection and the freedom left. Mirror parity: 1,377 configurations, each compared three ways (H, the construction line and the line against V). They cover every choice of fixed, expression-held and Fix-held points, alone, beside an Equal or with a conflict planted 0.5 mm along the mirror. Lines are also squared to the mirror, one or both, and radii are fixed alike on A, on B or on both, alone or beside Equal. Every one agrees in result, reason, message, freedom, conflicting, redundant and partly redundant ids, issues and definition, across solved, redundant, conflicting and failed outcomes. The failed outcome is the lens whose ends collapse at a stall. Refusals cover two kinds, one curve twice, a mirror that is not a line, an axis among the curves, circles on one centre, lines on the same two ends, arcs on the same three points, arcs sharing a start, an axis line end, and Equal of a line with an arc or circle. De-duplication and recognition: key order; applied with Remove ids; point Symmetrics of two lines applied; circles with a centre Symmetric and an Equal radius applied; Equal refused on curves that mirror. Also covered: names and meanings, an agent edit with the curve form, Trim removing the relation from an end trim and a circle trim, and Split and Extend refusing it. Existing tests touched: the offers (three lines also offer Symmetric; two circles on one centre give the circles reason), the registry (a curve Symmetric reference), the constraint tool (the Equal and circles reasons), the glyph layout (curve marks on both curves and the mirror line, none for an axis), the offer parity rules, and the precision role pin. Mutations before review, each restored, against cadSketchCurveSymmetry, the offer parity, both baselines, the registry, offers, symmetry relations, lowering, constraint tool and glyph layout suites (96 tests). Arcs of one direction paired start with start fails 7. Two point Symmetrics no longer counted as a line mirror fails 1. A key that keeps the curves in stored order fails 2. Circles without their equal-radius row fail 2 (these four ran on the first lowering). The equation baseline passes under each. Trim without the curve Symmetric removal fails the trim test, and a pairing tie of 0 fails the pairing test and the precision pin. Merge: main at 0.0.791 is merged, keeping 0.0.794 after 0.0.793. The pairing tie reads the new precision role to satisfy the precision literal check. Since review round 1. (1) Arcs lowered their second end pair as one row chosen from the geometry, so a solve could settle on the other crossing of the arcs’ circles. In the repro, arcs about V both counter-clockwise, A with centre (20,10), start (25,10), end (20,15) and B with centre (-20,10), start (-20,15), end (-15,10), the solve settled on another branch instead of the true mirror. Every pair now lowers whole, so arcs give 6 rows for 5 freedoms; the rows yield, and a pair that does not reflect starts the second curve’s point at the first’s image. The repro solves to B’s end at (-25,10). A sweep covers 1,152 arc pairs: V or a fixed line; two centres; radii 3 and 6; starts at 0, 100, 190 and 280 degrees; sweeps of 60 and 200 degrees; both directions; c1 and s1 each free, expression-fixed or held by Fix; and A’s radius, B’s or neither fixed to 7. Each one solves to the true mirror (640) or is rejected (512); none solves anywhere else. (2) The mirror yields to the rest of the sketch, so two lines kept Horizontal mirror about V. The freedom left counts only what the mirror adds, and nothing is reported redundant that is not. The planner refuses lines whose directions the mirror cannot keep. When the mirror’s, A’s and B’s directions are all fixed, it compares 2θM − θA with θB modulo π within CAD_PRECISION.angularAccuracyRad. When Parallel, Perpendicular, Collinear, Horizontal or Vertical tie A to B, it compares their parity. The reason names the relations, for example: “The Horizontal and Vertical relations keep these lines in directions that cannot mirror about the V axis. Remove one of them first.” A matrix puts none, Horizontal or Vertical on each of A and B, about H, V, a free construction line drawn near V and a line fixed at 120 degrees. It gives 26 applied, 8 refused by name, and 2 the free line cannot reach from near V. Those 2 fail the graph check and are never solved wrongly; with the line drawn near the bisector, they solve with freedom 6. Removing the Horizontal or Vertical afterwards leaves the whole mirror with freedom 8 or 4, and nothing moves. Beside Parallel, Perpendicular or Collinear, Equal, point Symmetrics, holds on the H axis and a shared end on the mirror, each case solves with the exact freedom. Four direction conflicts are refused. (3) Fixed radii mirror when they are equal: a circle radius expression, a constant radius or diameter size, or an arc with its centre and an end fixed, on A, on B or on both. Circles keep freedom 2, arcs 4, and arcs fixed at two points each keep 0. When the fixed radii differ, the plan is refused with “These circles have fixed radii that differ, so they cannot mirror each other.” A sketch that stores the mirror anyway is rejected as conflicting, naming it. No general rule turns rows over only fixed parameters into checks. The mirror’s own rows of that kind yield, so they agree silently or conflict. A global rule would change the diagnosis of other relations and probably the baseline, so it was not added. (4) Where other relations keep part of a mirror, the curve Symmetric now joins them, so Equal is no longer skipped. The 11 cases are: half a line mirror, either way round; equal lines; both of those; a shared end on the mirror; equal circles; mirrored centres; mirrored arc centres; mirrored arc ends with equal arcs; equal arcs; and a shared arc end on the mirror. Each solves to the whole mirror with no redundancy. Equal on mirrored curves stays refused. Mutations, each restored, against cadSketchCurveSymmetry and the equation baseline (22 tests). The equation baseline passed under each. Arcs dropping one row of their last end pair fail 2. No seeding fails 2. The original defect, one row and no seeding, fails 4, including the repro. Rows that do not yield fail 7. Rows not deferred after other relations fail 2. No redundancy filter for yielding rows fails 6. No direction refusal fails 2. A circle radius row that does not yield fails 3. No fixed-radius refusal fails 1. Equal refused again in a partial mirror fails 2. The selectable-axes spec gains a test that draws two lines level with Create relations on, then makes them Symmetric about V from Constrain. Both Horizontal relations stay, B lands on A’s image, and the status reads Under defined · 3 DOF. Checks on the final tree. The full Vitest suite passed: 6,971 tests in 614 files, including the equation baseline and the discovery budget. No tool description changed, so discovery stays at 51,178 of 51,200 bytes. npm run build passed (tsc -b, vite build, docs build and check). Lint, with the precision literal check, has zero findings, and ui:check passed. check-release passed alone; against origin/main it fails only because 0.0.792 and 0.0.793 have not merged. The e2e project type-checks. Chromium specs on that build, each run alone with two workers: cad-sketch-selectable-axes 8, cad-sketch-constraints 28, cad-sketch-relation-glyphs 7 and cad-sketch-symmetry 1, all passed. On the first selectable-axes run, the circles test failed once: its removal poll read a version that went stale as the removal was accepted. It passed on three reruns. The poll now retries a stale read, and the run after that change passed. Deferred: Coradial, Rigid set and Equal spacing. The relation editor’s Symmetric centers checkbox is left to the panel work. No benchmark was run: nothing new runs on pointer moves.

publicNotes.summary: Points, lines, arcs and circles can be made symmetric about any line or axis.
changes: Select two lines, two arcs or two circles with a line or the H or V axis, in any order, and choose Symmetric to mirror them as whole curves.
Mirrored arcs and circles keep one radius, and mirrored lines may run either way.
Symmetric marks show on both curves and on the mirror line. Choose Symmetric again with the same selection to remove it.
Equal says why a line cannot be equal to an arc or circle.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged. Sketches with mirrored curves do not open in older releases.
